history.summary: CSV DUPLICATE FLAG: this row ('Enchey Monastery', Gangtok) is a DUPLICATE of CSV row 915 ('Enchey Monastery', Mangan) - both describe the same Nyingma Buddhist monastery standing ~3 km north-east of Gangtok in Gangtok district. Row 915 already corrects the CSV town to Gangtok. Deprecate one of the two rows; keep this cross-reference rather than listing twice. THIS IS A BUDDHIST MONASTERY (NYINGMA), NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. 'Enchey' means 'the solitary monastery'. It was founded by the tantrik Lama Druptob Karpo, a master said to have flying powers who blessed the site after flying from Maenam Hill and established a small gompa/hermitage there. FOUNDING-DATE FLAG: sources genuinely disagree - some give 1840 and others 1909 - treat as unresolved. The protecting deities are Khangchendzonga and Yabdean; legend says Guru Padmasambhava subdued spirits here. The prayer hall walls are covered with murals of the four cardinal-direction deities. About 90 Nyingma monks reside here.

town_description: Enchey stands on a forested hill ~3 km north-east of Gangtok, the capital of Sikkim, with the Kanchenjunga range visible from the complex. It is one of Gangtok's most-visited monasteries, easily combined with the nearby Flower Exhibition Centre and Ganesh Tok viewpoint.
tradition: Buddhism (Tibetan, Nyingma) - NOT a Hindu temple
